body: This needs to check for index or it will cause a segmentation fault, or the calling methods need to do so
This will fail on platforms not using SDL or if SDL is somehow not initialized, it also breaks encapsulation I'd say, this should be handled elsewhere

Hm, I think in this case we can add a new field to [`Input::Joypad`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/cb7cd815eeeb11aaa1f68453a515c76bec5ba73d/core/input/input.h#L167) class that determines if the joypad is known or not, we can set it in `Input::joy_connection_changed` based on the information from the joypad's Dictionary info or its mapping. Is this approach good enough? :D

That sounds good I'd say, not sure if the problem to solve is specific to SDL but if it's not it should be implemented in a general way so other input systems can work with it, but that sounds like a convenient way to present the data
Thanks for the suggestions. I will go a route of adding new field on `Input::Joypad` class

I think it can be changed to:
```suggestion
	return joy_names.has(p_device) && joy_names[p_device].is_known;
```

In this case we'll also need to make sure `mapping_handled` field only gets defined if `SDL_IsGamepad()` is true, see also: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/cb7cd815eeeb11aaa1f68453a515c76bec5ba73d/drivers/sdl/joypad_sdl.cpp#L189
I'm not sure if this is going to affect the joysticks' mappings, but I think it won't since if SDL can't find a mapping for the device, I think Godot won't either.

So is it possible that `mapping_handled = true` even if there is no valid mapping?

I can add condition here if necessary
```
// Skip Godot's mapping system if SDL already handles the joypad's mapping.
joypad_info["mapping_handled"] = SDL_IsGamepad(sdl_event.jdevice.which); 
```
Is seems to have no impact on method output and pad still works fine

```
Name: XInput Controller
GUID: 0300fa675e040000130b000017057801
INFO: { "raw_name": "Xbox Series X Controller", "vendor_id": "1118", "product_id": "2835", "xinput_index": "0" }

```

> So is it possible that mapping_handled = true even if there is no valid mapping?

That's how it currently works in master, yes
I noticed an unnecessary empty line :D

> but set_fallback_mapping can set valid mapping to fallback_mapping

The check looks reasonable, if it's using fallback mapping, it should not be considered known, even if the mapping is valid.
This isn't a hot path, so I wouldn't bother doing such micro-optimization which IMO hurts readability.

Given the above, the comment should likely be removed. It's better to not write comments in the codebase that express doubt about what the code does - these questions should be raised with review comments on the PR instead.
